Liam / Sofia — quick technical note and attachments attached (stubs below). Summary first, details after.

Summary (for procurement/security):
- Private deployment model for the EU pilot: we will deploy inference serving nodes exclusively in eu-west-1 (Ireland) for the pilot. No cross-region model serving will be provisioned for this binding.
- Private connectivity: we will use AWS PrivateLink endpoints in your VPC paired with a dedicated PrivateLink service in our dedicated EU cluster; traffic between AegisHealth and Redwood inference nodes traverses the PrivateLink interfaces and never routes over the public internet.
- Egress controls: outbound egress from serving nodes is blocked by default by security groups/NACLs; any required outbound (e.g., for OS patching) uses a restricted, audited NAT path in our EU maintenance VLAN with strict firewall rules and is logged.
- KMS/HSM: For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (customer KMS project/CMK plugged into our operator). HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM / KMS with HSM) are supported when customers provision and attach their key resources. Keys are stored in the customer's KMS in the eu-west-1 region; Redwood never exports raw key material. For the hosted path we use region-scoped Redwood KMS with HSM-backed providers and strict key access audit logs.
- Audit artifacts: audit logs for network flows and KMS access are retained for 90 days by default; retention can be extended as part of the enterprise package.

Attached (stubs):
- network-peering-eu-apac.pdf (diagram: PrivateLink endpoints, service ENIs, routing/NAT path; redacted IPs)
- CAIQ-Answers-AegisHealth.xlsx (partially completed answers; highlighted controls need legal input)
- soc2-report-redacted.pdf (redacted PDF with cover attestation; full report available under NDA if required)

If you need an explicit signed binding statement (short letter) on region locking + key placement for procurement I can draft one.

Technical detail (brief):
- Serving nodes are tagged and placement constrained to eu-west-1. We enforce placement during rollout; CI/CD checks prevent cross-region flips.
- PrivateLink service exposes an internal hostname served from the EU cluster; our router enforces inbound model-request validation, and we map tenant routing so AegisHealth traffic is pinned to the allocated EU node pool.
- KMS calls are proxied through the operator but the CMK operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) are executed against the customer's KMS endpoint in their account (customer provides read-only IAM principal for the operator to call the KMS with limited permissions). We log all KMS usage to the audit stream we share with customers.

Let me know if you want me to convert the above into a one-page letter for signature.

—Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
